stem: Why might a 'time and volume chart' be useful during the assessment of a child who wets the bed?

options.text: It can identify bladder spasms or reduced bladder capacity through frequent, small voids.
It measures the exact sugar levels in the urine to detect diabetes.
It determines if the child has a psychological fear of the dark.
It provides a reward system for the child to stay motivated.

explanation: Tracking the frequency and volume of urine helps clinicians see if the child's bladder is unable to hold normal amounts of urine.
rationale: This tool helps visualize the physical behavior and storage capability of the bladder.

optionExplanations.A: Tracking the frequency and volume of urine helps clinicians see if the child's bladder is unable to hold normal amounts of urine.
optionExplanations.B: While diabetes is a concern, a time and volume chart measures output levels, not chemical composition.
optionExplanations.C: Fear of the dark is assessed through history-taking, while the chart tracks physiological data.
optionExplanations.D: While tracking can be motivating, its primary clinical use is to provide data on bladder capacity and production frequency.

source.hint: This tool helps visualize the physical behavior and storage capability of the bladder.
